# Summary of the Green Party 2024 Manifesto

## Health and Social Care
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS expenditure by 2030, plus £20bn capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability, boosting staff pay, and investing £3bn annually in NHS dentistry by 2030. Mental health services would receive funding for 28-day access to therapies. Social care would receive £20bn annually, introducing free personal care and establishing career structures for care workers.

## Housing
The manifesto commits to 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would insulate homes to EPC B standard. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy and Climate
Proposals include wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, no new oil and gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and community ownership of energy sources. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would rise to £500 within ten years. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy and Taxation
The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual investment in green economic transformation. Water companies, railways, and major retail energy companies would return to public ownership. Tax reforms include a wealth tax (1% above £10m assets, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and introducing a carbon tax. These measures aim to raise £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.

## Work and Welfare
Proposals include a £15 minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and moving toward a four-day week. Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, disability benefits by 5%, and the two-child benefit cap would be abolished.

## Education
Commitments include £8bn school investment, £2bn teacher pay uplift, free school meals, abolishing tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and £5bn for special educational needs provision.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn. Railways would return to public ownership, local authorities would control buses, and £2.5bn annually would fund cycleways and footpaths. Petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Environment and Nature
The manifesto proposes a Rights of Nature Act, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, returning water companies to public ownership, and £1.5bn additional DEFRA funding. A Right to Roam Act would be introduced for England.

## Democratic Reform
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The manifesto calls for ending the hostile environment, establishing safe asylum routes, abolishing No Recourse to Public Funds conditions, and ending immigration detention except for public safety cases.

## Foreign Policy
Commitments include supporting Ukraine, calling for an Israel-Gaza ceasefire, recognising Palestine, raising overseas aid to 1% of GNI by 2033, working toward EU membership, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident.
